careerInfoDesignation: Member of the NBS Bank Board
educationInfo: Comenius University in Bratislava, Faculty of Management Master’s degree (Mgr.); Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania PhD in Finance
achievements: His research has earned several awards, including two Smith Breeden Prizes for the best paper of the year in The Journal of Finance, three Fama/DFA Prizes for the best paper of the year in the Journal of Financial Economics, the Barclays Global Investors Prize, the BlackRock Award, the Goldman Sachs Asset Management Award, and the NASDAQ Award. As at 1 January 2021 his work had more than 16,000 Google Scholar citations. For his teaching, Professor Pástor has received the McKinsey Award for Excellence in Teaching (2011) and two Faculty Excellence Awards from the University of Chicago (2009, 2010).
additionalInfo: Professor Pástor’s research activity has focused on various issues in the field of financial economics. His work covers topics such as the liquidity of financial markets, the effects of political uncertainty on financial markets, sustainable investment, stock price bubbles, technological revolutions, mutual fund performance, stock return predictability, long-horizon volatility, optimal portfolio choice, and quantitative easing. He has been published in top academic journals, including the American Economic Review, The Journal of Finance, the Journal of Financial Economics, the Journal of Monetary Economics, the Journal of Political Economy, and The Review of Financial Studies. Off-campus, Professor Pástor is involved with several non-profit academic organisations. Since 1 January 2021 he has been a director of the European Finance Association, and from 2016 to 2019 he was on the Board of Directors of the American Finance Association. He was on the Board of Directors of the Western Finance Association (WFA) from 2010 to 2017 and served as the WFA’s President from 2016 to 2017. He is a research associate with the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) and a research fellow with the Centre for Economic Policy Research (CEPR). From 2006 to 2017 he was a member of the Academic Advisory Board of the Gutmann Center at WU Vienna, and he has also served on the editorial boards of the Journal of Financial Economics (since 2006), The Journal of Finance (2006–2016), and The Review of Financial Studies (2006–2009). Besides his academic activities, Professor Pástor has co-designed new stock market indexes – CRSP Indexes – which are today tracked by index funds that together have more than one trillion US dollars’ worth of assets under management (among them is the world’s largest mutual fund). Professor Pástor has been a member of the NBS Bank Board since 15 March 2015.
